Bridges’s wardrobe, too, is ever-evolving—he still rocks plenty of killer vintage, but he’s also unafraid to dabble in designer grails from the likes of Celine and Nicholas Daley. GQ: How did you get your start in the music industry?

Leon Bridges: Actually, I started initially as a dancer. My first time ever being on a stage was through dance. I was blessed enough to run into a community of musicians who really helped. I always loved to sing, but they helped nurture my love for music and inspired me to pick up a guitar. I started doing open mics, and I met this cat named Austin Jenkins who pretty much saved my life. He offered to record these songs that I'd been writing and we put it on SoundCloud, and everything just snowballed from there. That was in 2014.
Is there anything you haven't done that's still on your musical bucket list?

Man, yeah. The crazy thing is I think I've hit all the milestones. I have collaborated with some of my favorite artists. Next thing I want to do is a Muscle Shoals thing—just get a collective of musicians and help aspiring musicians record some music.

You’ve had plenty of incredible experiences in your career, from performing in the White House with the Obamas to opening for the Rolling Stones on tour. Do you have a favorite moment you can recount?

It had to have been going to Obama’s birthday party. I’m just like, “Whoa, that’s George Lucas. That’s Paul McCartney.” Man, so surreal. It’s just a reflection of making good art and keeping at it and having integrity.

Bridges’s wardrobe, too, is ever-evolving—he still rocks plenty of killer vintage, but he’s also unafraid to dabble in designer grails from the likes of Celine and Nicholas Daley. Below, I caught up with the musician to chat through his pre-show rituals, his go-to Bode jacket, and the wildest moment of his career.

Jacket by Bode. Jeans by Celine. Vintage boots by Campus.
